cards.title: Why agentic evaluation datasets are fundamentally different — and how to build them right
cards.excerpt: Multi-step agent evaluation requires a new approach to data design. We break down the key differences from single-turn annotation and share lessons from dozens of agentic training projects.

cards.title: Red-teaming at scale: lessons from 5,000 adversarial prompts
cards.excerpt: Building effective safety datasets means understanding what makes an adversarial prompt genuinely dangerous — not merely surprising.

cards.title: The hidden complexity of mathematical reasoning datasets
cards.excerpt: Building useful math training data requires careful attention to notation, proof style, error taxonomy, and solution diversity.

cards.title: Inter-annotator agreement: what it really tells you about data quality
cards.excerpt: IAA scores are widely cited but poorly understood. We explain what Cohen's κ measures — and what it misses in complex annotation tasks.

cards.title: What makes a great preference annotator? Insights from 1,000 calibration tasks
cards.excerpt: We analysed calibration data from over a thousand annotators to identify what predicts high-quality RLHF feedback.

cards.title: The data flywheel: how training data quality compounds over model generations
cards.excerpt: The quality of data you build today shapes the capabilities of models trained years from now. We explore the long-term flywheel.

cards.title: Building coding task environments that actually test agent capability
cards.excerpt: Most code evaluation environments are too clean. Real software engineering tasks are messy and ambiguous. Here's how we design for that.
